in writing. the aim of this agreement is to replace certain provisions of the 47 existing bilateral air services agreements between the member states and the west african economic and monetary union. it is appropriate to harmonize the various provisions of existing agreements by means of a community agreement of a horizontal type. it will restore legal certainty to bilateral air services agreements concluded between the member states of the waemu and the european union and will also avoid harming member states which have not signed a bilateral agreement with one of the waemu states. it will avoid discrimination between carriers in the designation or taxation of aviation fuel. the provisions of bilateral agreements which are anti-competitive shall be brought into line with european competition law. the agreement will strengthen euro-african air transport relations and promote cooperation between the european union and the union of african states on aviation, including safety and security.
in writing. the recent humanitarian disasters in haiti and pakistan have once again demonstrated the need to strengthen the eu's disaster response capacity in terms of efficiency, coordination and visibility. that is why i voted in favour of this report, which calls for the creation of a european rapid reaction capability (a european civil protection force) - an idea which was launched by commissioner michel barnier at the time of the asian tsunami and since then repeatedly taken up by the european parliament. this capacity should be an optimisation of the available tools, which would gain in efficiency and visibility, with the aim of achieving an immediate mobilisation of all the necessary means, through enhanced cooperation.
in writing. the humanitarian environment is increasingly complex and unwieldy: humanitarian law is often violated, confused roles mean that humanitarian workers are increasingly targeted, and natural disasters are increasing in number and intensity. in 2010, we witnessed the three biggest humanitarian disasters in recent years: the earthquake in haiti, the drought in the sahel and the floods in pakistan. but as commissioner kristalina georgieva said, 'the quality of our humanitarian aid is of the utmost importance'. it "saves some 140 million lives every year". in view of these considerations, i agree with the rapporteur when she advocates a substantial increase in the funding of humanitarian aid and when she states that the humanitarian consensus is too little known. the need to continue to raise awareness and promote humanitarian principles and international law. as i have already said, we must advocate the creation of a european rapid reaction capability. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full.
in writing. worldwide, 900 million people suffer from chronic hunger as a result of extreme poverty. despite apparently sufficient food supplies, a significant proportion of the world's population cannot afford the basic necessities of life. the availability of food is a vital issue that must be addressed! the objective of food security cannot be achieved without addressing two of the most important issues facing us today: the volatility of markets and prices and the decline in food stocks. in this context, it is necessary to advocate a revision of the current legislation on financial instruments, which should increase the transparency of trade and provide for minimum thresholds for operators admitted to intervene in these markets. moreover, the world's food supply of basic necessities is much more limited than it has ever been, with the world's food reserves at an all-time low! finally, the cap must provide an unequivocal response to food security and other challenges, including climate change and the economic crisis in the eu.
in writing. - overall, this report is a fairly good contribution to the debate on the role of agriculture in the food supply. the ep rightly points out the problems faced by farmers in times of extreme market and price volatility and draws attention to the difficulties faced by farmers in this respect. the commission must come up with lasting and strong measures to address the volatility in agricultural markets. this is crucial for the maintenance of union production. the enormous price increases on the financial markets for agricultural commodities are largely the result of speculation. speculative behavior accounts for almost 50% of recent price increases. the ep welcomes the conclusions of the un special rapporteur on the right to food on the nefarious role of large institutional investors such as hedge funds, pension funds and investment banks in influencing commodity price indices through their movements in derivatives markets. the ep is making a good analysis, but it is going completely off the rails by making irrelevant comments in the report on the role of gmos in agricultural policy. this debate is being held elsewhere and does not belong here. that is why i voted against the report in the end.

in writing. the issue of crossborder healthcare had been under negotiation for a long time but had raised a shield when, in a previous version, the risk of creating a two-speed medicine appeared, promoting mainly the medical tourism of the most affluent patients and harming member states which could not have planned their care provision according to a demand conditioned by the quality offered ... the text we voted on wednesday is more consensual. it allows european patients to benefit from care that is not available in their country or is only available for very long periods of time. the reimbursement of such care received in another member state is made in the country where the patient is registered but is capped at what would have been paid for similar care... some specialised care or treatment requiring overnight hospitalization will require prior authorisation. but any refusal will have to be justified. this is another step towards a more concrete europe of health. we can only be happy about that.
in writing. - i welcome the directive on patients' rights in crossborder healthcare. the provision of patient-oriented healthcare as quickly as possible, which can also be used in other member states, is an essential prerequisite for the cohesion of the eu area. in particular, in border regions like the one i come from, cross-border healthcare is a daily reality. in this context, i am very pleased about the facilitation of access to reliable and high-quality cross-border healthcare and reimbursement. i am particularly in favour of the added value for patients on waiting lists, because this new regulation gives them the opportunity to have treatment in another member state in good time, whereas they would only be entitled to this treatment with a considerable delay in their own member state. while the establishment of the grounds for refusal for prior authorisation is also very useful and provides more clarity, some border healthcare problems remain unresolved, especially for long-term border crossers who, after their active life, have to renounce all or part of the services important to them in the country of work.
in writing. - the crossborder healthcare directive - which i support - gives clear rights to patients to receive medical care abroad and to be reimbursed according to domestic rates. this will increase legal certainty for patients in border regions, people residing in another country, patients with rare diseases and patients facing long waiting times. however, in order to safeguard the quality of care and fair access to it, member states may require patients to obtain prior consent to treatment. this is required when hospitalization is involved or when treatment is very expensive or risky. the reimbursement may also be refused under very strict conditions (for example, if treatment is also possible in one's own country). and member states can intervene if there is evidence of overconsumption. the directive thus maintains the balance between the right of the patient to good health care and the right of the member states to finance their own social security and to organise their own health care. i also hope that the desire of patients to seek treatment elsewhere will not put undue pressure on the high-quality services that the vast majority of patients choose in their own country.

rapporteur. − mr president, these days competition is often regarded as a concept that makes life difficult. some people prefer cosy arrangements and the hot tub of backstage agreements as protection against the harsh world of global competition. but, commissioner, competition is not the spoiler but the lifesaver of the european economy. europe is at a crossroads. will it create a transfer economy, with low growth and high structural unemployment, or will it have a wealth-creating economy that stands the test of global competition? a football team, commissioner, that is not competitive loses game after game. an economy that is not competitive loses investment, jobs and finally the basis of its social arrangements. since european competition policy is the exclusive competence of the european commission, you, commissioner – or rather commissioner almunia, for whom you are standing in – play a decisive role. this week the united nations published figures on foreign direct investment in 2010. the united states attracted 43% more foreign investment than in 2009. foreign direct investment in latin america rose by 21% and in asia by 10%. in the european union it dropped by 20% – and why is that? the money goes to where the action is. apparently investors regard europe as the continent of inaction, only generating poor growth figures. it demonstrates the european union facing a competitiveness deficit. commissioner, you have to assure a level playing field for entrepreneurial activity in europe to make our continent fit for global competition. we all know china. i would like to draw your attention to several aspects of competition policy in 2009, of which many features are visible today. the main issue now is the consequences of massive state aid to the financial sector: states allocated taxpayers’ money to prevent the collapse of the financial sector. had we allowed a meltdown of the financial sector, the savings and pensions of millions of european citizens would have been buried too. but it goes without saying that state aid on this scale created distortions of competition. that is why it has to end as soon as possible and the money has to be paid back to taxpayers in europe. commissioner, my first question therefore is: how temporary is the temporary framework, and how will it be phased out? i hope you will clarify this issue on behalf of commissioner almunia. another aspect is liquidity support of the european central bank to certain banks in order to keep them alive. i admit there is an interface between monetary and competition policy – but did its impact distort competition? that is my question. another issue is the set of rules for divestment. work criteria for downsizing companies are sufficiently clear and fair. now we should look at the future: what is going to happen, commissioner? member states have gone very far to recapitalise the financial sector by partly and/or entirely nationalising institutions with taxpayers’ money. this will have to be unravelled. but once member states start withdrawing from financial institutions to restore their private status, there is a danger that they will leave behind a dowry, a sort of wedding gift. dowries may be used to prop up the position of financial institutions in the private market. this is a feature we have often seen in the process of privatisation. i remember it too well in the postal sector. governments propped up their postal provider just before entering the private market. in a letter i reminded commissioner almunia of the long-lasting investigation into the german postal provider. the commission is currently opening investigations into the british, french and belgian postal providers as well, since these postal markets will be liberalised this year. so, commissioner, i ask you to be attentive to the phenomenon of dowry in the financial sector. preventing a problem is better than going the long way of legal redress. i thank you, commissioner – and also commissioner almunia – for your cooperation, and i also thank the service of dg competition which, as i know, is one of the best in the commission.

in writing. the arctic region is attracting increasing attention because of the effects of climate change, the main driver of its evolution. the european union is a major contributor to climate change and must therefore play a leading role in combating it. due to the growing need for natural resources, in particular in the union, the arctic represents a significant and varied potential in terms of energy supply (gas, renewable energy), raw materials and fish. the european union must commit itself to policies that take account of the sustainable management and exploitation of the region's natural resources in terms of environment, security and management. the application of iceland for membership highlights the need for a coordinated arctic policy at european level. it is up to the european union to strike a balance between environmental concerns and the race to exploit natural resources, and to take account of the interests of the people of the arctic region.
in writing. the strategic importance of the black sea is no longer to be demonstrated today. the new frontier of the european union since the accession of bulgaria and romania, it represents an obvious geostrategic space. the eu is called upon to be directly and permanently involved in this. turkey, georgia and ukraine have repeatedly expressed their appetite for europe. the commission responded by launching its communication in 2007 on 'black sea synergy'. the latter, while ensuring stability in the region, responds to the requests of the states for both a euro-atlantic anchorage and a framework for enhanced cooperation. the eu must continue along this path. it must step up its involvement in the black sea to demonstrate its diplomatic soft power. in this way, the eu will ensure the construction of an area of peace, stability and prosperity, as well as the certainty of the security of the eu's energy supply.

in writing. i voted in favour of the recommendation for the second reading of the development cooperation instrument. i would also like to stress that the european parliament has always been in favour of granting financial measures for the banana sector to the ten acp banana-producing countries. the only sticking point in this case is the horizontal question of delegated acts. i hope that we can reach an agreement on this last point at institutional level in the near future. it is hardly acceptable that the countries receiving these amounts should not be able to use them. this delay undermines the credibility of our commitments and undermines the conclusion of the economic partnership agreements.
in writing. these agreements put an end to more than 15 years of dispute between europe and the banana-producing countries of latin america and the united states, which denounced the preferential treatment accorded by the europeans to the exports of the acp countries (africa, the caribbean and the pacific). the european union will now gradually reduce its customs duties on banana exports from latin america. on the other hand, bananas from the acp countries will continue to enjoy duty-free access to the european union. in addition, the main acp banana-producing countries will receive support from the eu budget (up to eur 200 million) to help them adapt to the increased competition from latin america. however, particular care will have to be taken to ensure that the agreement does not cause damage to small producers by strengthening the monopoly position of the large us multinationals which control the banana market in latin american countries. these agreements will have to be subject to an impact study on their effect on producers in developing countries and the outermost regions of the european union.
in writing. the amount of waste electrical and electronic equipment is increasing every year and therefore raises a number of health and environmental issues in the event of disposal or improper reprocessing. all these devices - computers, televisions, mobile phones and appliances - also waste scarce raw materials. today, only a third of this waste is properly collected and treated. this proportion should therefore be increased. the proposed text addresses several aspects of ensuring the proper disposal of electrical and electronic waste, whether in terms of the collection rate (85 per cent of the waste collected), the purpose of collection, consumer responsibility, the type of equipment or standards for collection, treatment and recycling. it is equally important to avoid illegal transfer outside the european union, particularly to developing countries. the increase in collection points should make it easier for citizens to dispose of their waste. it is a further step in the direction of protecting the environment and human health.
in writing. eight years after the adoption of the waste electrical and electronic equipment directive, the european parliament is once again taking a stand on the important issue of recycling waste high-tech products. and despite undeniable improvements in the treatment, recovery and disposal of this type of waste (an average drop of 20 kilograms of water per citizen in the ocean from the 5.8 tonnes of waste produced per year per european), progress still needs to be made. i therefore welcome the adoption this afternoon of the florence report, which reinforces the european commission's objective of achieving an eu-wide collection rate of 85% and a recycling rate of 50% to 75% by 2016, depending on the category of waste. how important it is, for example, to recover the valuable materials contained in a whole range of equipment: one ton of gsm contains about 280 grams of gold and 140 grams of platinum and palladium! it is common sense put to the service of environmental protection. in the same spirit, i supported the exclusion of solar panels from the directive for five years. it seems to me that this is a great way to promote this clean technology.

vice-president of the commission. − mr president, the legislative proposal on the rights of passengers travelling by bus and by coach that we are discussing today is the result of a very difficult process, including conciliation. long negotiations on the night of 30 november 2010 at the conciliation committee led to a breakthrough and a compromise after more than two years of negotiations. let endorsement by the council on 31 january, i invite you to also adopt this regulation and formally conclude the procedure. the proposal on the rights of passengers travelling by bus and coach now completes the arrangements for the protection of travellers and will ensure that passengers benefit from the same basic standards of service quality wherever they travel in the union. the compromise text contains important achievements: it provides a set of basic rights for all passengers travelling by bus and coach. as mr cancian has already mentioned, there were difficult points unresolved until the last moment of negotiations. some may say that the scope of the regulation on bus and coach services of 250 kms and more is too limited and they would have wished to see passengers in local potential cost implications for the industry have been kept to a minimum. all in all, the compromise text constitutes a real advance for travelling citizens and for the image of the industry.

in writing. in december 2008, the commission presented a proposal for a regulation on passenger rights in bus and coach transport. the main objective of this proposal was to establish common provisions on passenger rights in bus and coach transport. now it is done, and i am glad of it: passengers travelling at least 250 km by bus now have the same rights throughout the eu to information, assistance and compensation in the event of cancellation, overbooking and delay of at least two hours. passengers must be given the choice between reimbursement of the ticket price or continuing the journey under the same conditions and without additional charges. if reimbursement is the only option available, compensation of 50% of the ticket price should be granted. in addition, in the event of loss or damage to luggage, passengers will be entitled to compensation.
in writing. i abstained on this regulation on passenger rights in bus transport, which was voted by a large majority of socialists/conservatives. i regret the considerable backsliding from the position originally adopted by our parliament on three main points. 1. the only distances greater than 250 km will be covered. in practice, the passenger on a brussels-amsterdam bus journey will not be protected, whereas the one on an airplane will be! this is unfair, especially when we consider that it is often the less privileged who use this mode of transport. 2. the the force majeure clause (bad weather or natural disaster) may be too easily invoked by bus operators to circumvent compensation to passengers in the event of delay or cancellation. 3. the the derogations will allow those states which so wish to postpone the entry into force of this regulation until 2021! i am, however, pleased with the progress made in the text: compulsory assistance for disabled persons and persons with reduced mobility, rights and compensation in the event of accidents, delays or cancellations. but parliament has settled for a badly-constructed rebate agreement. except in exceptional cases, the scope of these rights will be considerably limited, to the detriment of bus passengers.
in writing. this is the fourth package on safeguarding passenger rights. after a regulation on the rights of passengers in air, rail and water transport, we now deal with the rights of bus passengers. they will now be compensated for travel delays of more than 250 kilometres, assisted in cancelling trips, protected in the event of accidents and deaths and reimbursed for lost or damaged belongings. passengers with reduced mobility will also be entitled to special assistance, as is already the case with airlines. the ep's position at first and second readings was substantially weakened. the ep wanted to apply the rules to journeys of more than 50 kilometres. the council only wanted it for journeys longer than 500 kilometres. the compromise was 150 miles. this means that they do not apply to routes which are commonly used, such as brussels-amsterdam, luxembourg-strasbourg or vienna-budapest. it is good that this legislation provides a list of 12 basic rules - valid for any distance - that focus on the needs of disabled people and other people with reduced mobility. nevertheless, the green group is very disappointed with the very weak result achieved. that is why i am voting against this agreement with the green group.

in writing. − reducing co2 emissions is desirable for all modes of transport, including small goods vehicles. the setting of limit values is important in order to achieve an ambitious approach among vehicle manufacturers. the agreement on the limit values is due, among other things, to the negotiating skills of the belgian presidency. this compromise includes a short-term target of 175 g/km in 2014. it also sets a phase-down target, with a long-term target of 147 g/km by 2020. these objectives are accompanied by measures to encourage industry to build energy-efficient commercial vehicles. the achievement of these objectives will not only benefit small and mediumsized enterprises, which are the main users of sprinters and vans, but also private individuals and, last but not least, the environment. we will have a say not only at eu level but also in the world market tomorrow if we produce safe and clean vehicles. we should also not allow our expertise to be exported to other countries - such as china - by hesitant eu policies, but use it as a way to shape a sustainable european environmental policy that has a positive impact not only on europe's industrial base, but also on employment. i welcome the compromise reached and have therefore supported it.

in writing. - i fully support the initial proposal to set co2 emission standards for new light commercial vehicles to avoid a regulatory gap due to certain overlaps between the registrations of passenger cars and commercial vehicles. at present, many vehicles type-approved as passenger cars, such as suvs, are registered as light commercial vehicles, often because the latter category is taxed less heavily or enjoys other tax benefits. although the legislation on passenger cars (and this proposal) is based on the type-approval of the vehicles (and not on registration), the lack of legislation on light commercial vehicles risks that manufacturers would apply for type-approval as a light commercial vehicle for larger passenger cars. this would mean that the co2 emission standards would not apply to these high-emission vehicles. the first reading agreement has turned out to be a very weak agreement, postponing the binding target of 175 g co2/km by one year. the 2020 target is set at 147 g/km and the fines for non-compliance are reduced from eur 120/gram to eur 95/gram. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the environmental impact of the proposed legislation is not underestimated. the sense of urgency is gone, that much is clear. that is why i am voting no.

50% of medicines sold on the internet and 1-3% of medicines sold in pharmacies are counterfeit. these falsifications are evolving, affecting not only comfort medicines but also life-saving medicines. we must protect the health of our citizens who, for reasons of economy or time, order from the internet without realising that they are in danger. and when those fake drugs get into the official supply chain and end up in the pharmacy, they can cost any of us our lives. 200,000 people die every year worldwide from ingesting fake medicines. it is not only a problem of concern, but a scourge against which we must fight with all our strength. that is why i welcome the forthcoming adoption of this directive, which will create a unique traceability identifier to verify the authenticity of medicines and a common logo to identify safe websites offering the sale of medicines at a distance. i would like to stress one point, however: the patient's right to security cannot be used as a pretext for increasing prices.
member of the commission. − allow me to address each of the four component questions in turn. the first question was: can the commission explain why a decision was not taken in 1998 to ban the marketing of pharmaceuticals containing benfluorex? the answer: benfluorex was discussed in 1998 in the committee for proprietary medicinal products, now called the committee for medical products for human use, of the european medicines agency, and subsequently in the pharmacovigilance working party. the committee considered that benfluorex should not be included in the scope of an ongoing evaluation procedure at european level, concerning certain anorectic agents due to a different mode of action. however, it was agreed that the committee’s pharmacovigilance working party would investigate if there was a safety issue with this compound. in march 1999, the pharmacovigilance working party concluded that there were no major benefit-risk concerns for medicinal products containing benfluorex. further discussion in the working party did not lead to changes in this conclusion. the second question: should the commission not have been alerted and not first by the bans imposed by the authorities in spain and italy? the answer: italy and spain did not revoke the marketing authorisation for benfluorex. in fact, the first time that a member state effectively took measures to revoke the national marketing authorisation for mediator was in 2009, when france suspended its national marketing authorisation. in spain it was the marketing authorisation holder, servier, that withdrew the marketing authorisation in 2003. similarly, it was servier itself that did not request the renewal of the marketing authorisation in 2003 in italy. the product remained authorised in france, portugal, luxembourg and greece. benfluorex was discussed within the pharmacovigilance working party, acting in its role as a forum for member states to exchange pharmacovigilance data among themselves. i would like to clarify that monitoring of pharmacovigilance data and the subsequent decision-making on national authorisations for medicinal products is the primary responsibility of member states. commission intervention in these cases is exceptional and limited to concrete situations foreseen in the legislation. the commission can launch a europe-wide evaluation by the european medicines agency in two cases: firstly, when member states adopt divergent national decisions concerning a marketing authorisation and, secondly, before any decision is reached on the granting, variation, suspension or revocation of a marketing authorisation that appears necessary, in particular when taking account of pharmacovigilance information in cases where it considers that the interests of the community are involved. in this case no action was triggered at eu level in the light of the conclusions of the pharmacovigilance working party and the fact that no divergent decisions were taken at the time by the member states in response to the discussions in the working party. the third question was: why did the commission not act until as late as june 2010 when it finally took a clear decision on the marketing of that molecule? the answer: it was only in 2009 that a member state, namely france, suspended the marketing authorisation of mediator. under the new provisions in place since 2004 this automatically triggered a review of the product’s benefit-risk balance, which led to the adoption of a commission decision requiring all member states to revoke any national authorisations for benfluorex containing medicinal products. in this context it is important to stress that the new pharmacovigilance legislation adopted on 15 december 2010 introduced additional provisions to ensure signal detection by the european medicines agency of safety issues for nationally-authorised products and creates new procedures at eu level to assess safety signals for such products, leading to harmonised actions by the member states. the fourth and last question was: will the commission ask the european medicines agency to conduct a full retrospective investigation into the ways in which this drug was used over 20 years? the answer: to date the commission has not asked the european medicines agency to conduct a full retrospective investigation into the ways in which this medicinal product was used over 20 years. the figures and the documentation referred to in the french report clearly indicate that by far the highest use of this medicinal product was in france.
madam president, commissioner, let us broaden the debate, since the case of the mediator is only the visible part of the iceberg that raises many other questions. for example, why can any medicine, considered potentially dangerous and even deadly, which has been withdrawn from the market in some member states, continue to circulate freely within the european union? should we not reflect on the role and effectiveness of the european medicines agency, since its conclusions are not binding on the member states?
member of the commission. − in effect, the procedures that were in force at the time of the historic events that i recounted in my answer were as i stated: there was a clear separation between member states and the european authority – a separation that is still in fact in force and jealously guarded by member states. in effect that is why, over time, we feel that we should be strengthening our pharmacovigilance processes and procedures. i must say that, in 2004, a step forward was taken on revising the pharmacovigilance procedures and processes that we already have, and also in the last pharmacovigilance agreement. we now have a lot of ‘stoppers’ and it is now also possible for other action to be taken at european level, too, to ensure that anything that is withdrawn from any market is notified and action can be taken upon it. this was not the case before. so this is the situation today. i have instructed my services to conduct a stress test now, including on the new pharmacovigilance processes and procedures put in place after our last agreement. they are taking médiator as a case study to see whether something like médiator could still happen with the latest pharmacovigilance processes. we will make sure that if we do find any vacuums, bottlenecks or spaces where action will not be taken in these cases, we will come back to you and try to correct the situation.
member of the commission. − apple announced today that it will offer digital subscriptions to newspapers and magazines on ipad devices exclusively through applications (apps) sold via its online store. publishers will still be able to offer online subscriptions through their websites or by other means but they will no longer be able to process the subscription via an app on an iphone using apple as an intermediary. whether apple’s behaviour constitutes a violation of the eu competition rules depends on a range of factual, legal and economic elements. it requires inter alia that apple holds a dominant position in the relevant market. the boundaries of such relevant markets are not clear, as the sector is still relatively new and evolving and as there are also several comparable platforms and devices that provide similar functionalities. some of which are supported by online application stores as the consumer demand for electronic and/or print magazines is unclear and evolving. once the market has been properly identified, the question of dominance would have to be assessed. dominance has been defined by the european court of justice as a position of economic strength enjoyed by an undertaking which enables it to hinder the maintenance of effective competition on the relevant market by allowing it to behave to an appreciable extent independently of its competitors and customers and ultimately of consumers. the commission notes in particular that alternative application platforms exist and several companies have recently launched, or are expecting to launch in the near future, a number of devices similar in terms of functionality to the ipad. the commission is following the developments regarding apple’s commercial policies and is in close contact with the national competition authorities.
apple has indeed announced this afternoon that it intends to offer a new model to subscribers, but it is clear that it intends to use its position - whether dominant or not - in the market to gain access to the customer information available to publishers. this could be very damaging in the long term for publishers in europe, and also damaging for media pluralism. i would therefore ask you whether you are prepared to act, whether you are in a dominant position or not, and if you wish to take any initiative, whether you can make clear what timing you have in mind. is it a matter of weeks or months before the commission takes any initiative in this area?

in writing. the europe 2020 strategy is ambitious, particularly in terms of employment, and the implementation of the employment guidelines is helping to achieve it. its objectives are fundamental, especially to enable pensions to be financed and to build a european social model based on welfare. the elements which could form the basis of this social model have been called into question by the proposals of mrs merkel and mr sarkozy. one of the proposals in the competitiveness pact is the abolition of automatic indexation of wages to inflation. the argument is that this would increase competitiveness and hence employment. there is no evidence that this reasoning is automatically true. the abolition of automatic indexation could even create in some cases phenomena of acceleration of inflation, which nobody wants. there are many other ways of fighting for employment, such as strategic investments or training in sectors of the future. the indexation of wages and social benefits is a well understood instrument by some countries to reduce the risk of poverty among workers, a growing phenomenon in europe. this will help to achieve another eu target for 2020: 20 million fewer poor people.

in writing. i voted in favour of this report because its objective is to combat counterfeit medicines in the legal supply chain at eu level without hampering the functioning of the internal market in medicines. for example, by introducing obligations for actors in the distribution chain; prohibiting the players between the original manufacturer and the last player in the distribution chain (usually the pharmacist) or the end user (physician/patient) from tampering (i.e. removing, changing or covering) with the safety features on the packaging; the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a directive on the protection of the health of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work.
in writing. as president jacques chirac said, 'the most intolerable inequality is inequality in health'. that is why i voted in favour of this report, which is aimed at health and therefore consumer protection. counterfeit drugs have long been a neglected scourge. while developing countries are an obvious target, because the price of legal medicines is often out of reach for most people and controls are ineffective or non-existent, counterfeit medicines are increasingly found in the eu, particularly via the internet. it's a growing threat to public health, to public safety, all over the world. the eu must remain vigilant and vigorously pursue a proactive policy against this unacceptable unveiling. its economic implications are currently difficult to quantify, as production has become industrialised. it is a moral problem, an ethical problem that undermines the credibility and efficiency of health systems. as such, the fight against counterfeit medicines must be a matter of conscience for political leaders worldwide.
in writing. after branded products and cigarettes, counterfeiting has taken over the pharmaceutical market, and the seven million medicinal products seized each year represent about 5% of all counterfeits. the challenge for european authorities, both judicial and customs, is enormous: to restore the supply chains and to curb this trade, which endangers the lives of millions of people worldwide. i therefore welcome the agreement reached between parliament and the council establishing a common legal framework for the 27 member states to limit the risk of falsification of medicines. among the main advances i would like to mention: the principle of cascading responsibility covering all actors in the chain, manufacturing authorization holders, wholesalers, brokers, etc.; the compulsory indication on the packaging of prescription medicines of a safety device (serial number or stamp); the introduction of stricter rules on inspections in cooperation with the european medicines agency; and the establishment of a list of entities authorised to carry out distance sales. in conclusion, this is important legislation, but it will require even more international cooperation and cyber-controls to eradicate fake viagra, slimming products, skin creams, etc., available with a simple click of the mouse.
in writing. − there is a worrying increase in the number of falsified medicines in the eu. they may contain inferior, adulterated or incorrectly dosed active or inactive ingredients or no active ingredients at all, and thus pose a serious threat to the patient. the direct and indirect social costs of non-action to business are certainly more than eur 10 billion. i support this agreement with the green group in the ep. it updates existing rules and introduces safety features to guarantee the identification, authentication and traceability of the medicinal product, while also regulating the sale of medicinal products via the internet. this is one of the main routes by which counterfeit medicines enter the european market. it is estimated that over 50% of medicines bought on the internet from sites that do not provide their actual physical address are counterfeit. therefore, a distinction should be made between legal mail order or internet pharmacies and the illegal distribution chain, which includes uncontrolled internet purchases. a legal mail order pharmacy should be associated with a legally registered pharmacy, ensuring that the legal mail order pharmacy complies with all the legal requirements applicable to pharmacies in the member state in which they are legally established.
in writing. small and medium-sized enterprises make a fundamental contribution to growth, social cohesion and play a crucial role in maintaining and expanding employment. however, the difficulty for smes to access finance is a major obstacle to their creation and growth, and the current economic crisis has exacerbated this problem. banks are increasingly reluctant to finance high-risk business ventures, innovative products or business transfers. the functioning of sme financing arrangements should therefore be strengthened, the continued implementation of guarantee instruments supported and the financing of innovative financial instruments increased. companies must have better access to financial instruments based on equity contributions. the complexity of financial regulations and the burden of bureaucracy also constitute a brake on the development of smes and it is therefore important to remove administrative barriers and to propose simpler and less costly regulations and guidelines.
in writing. − the demographic shift towards an ageing society, combined with the economic and financial crisis-induced setbacks in economic growth, public finances and financial markets, require an adjustment in pension policy. this adjustment is consistent with the completion of the european internal market and the europe 2020 objectives on employment and the sustainability of public finances. but above all i welcome this proposal because it provides for more efficient supply systems which are to be both sustainable and safe. i firmly believe that pension systems should not only provide older eu citizens with a decent life, but also be the reward for a lifetime of work. if we want european citizens to be motivated to work and open to cross-border activities in the future, it is important to offer them a reasonable and sustainable retirement income today, which is harmonised at european level. however, the responsibility for pension systems remains with the member states, which means that pension systems are primarily the responsibility of the member states and therefore only a coordinating guide should be given to the member states at european level. in this context, particular attention should be paid to the principle of solidarity between generations and the principle of national solidarity. even in the face of subsidiarity, all pension systems should remain 'exportable' for citizens.
in writing. according to the commissioner for employment, social affairs and inclusion, lászló andor, the number of pensioners will double by 2060 compared to the working population able to finance pensions. it is therefore urgent to look at the future of pension systems. although this is a matter for the member states, it should not prevent the european union from assisting the member states in their reflection on how to ensure that european citizens have an adequate, stable and sustainable pension system. the principle of free movement of persons is complemented by the possibility of obtaining a sufficient and appropriate pension in an eu member state. the economic and monetary crisis has demonstrated the need for an integrated approach, covering both economic and financial aspects as well as demographic and social aspects.
in writing. sustaining pension schemes is one of the major challenges facing the political class if it is to maintain the common good and social peace. and even though european competence in this area is limited, it was important that the european parliament gave its opinion in the follow-up to the green paper launched by the commission. this was done with the adoption of the very comprehensive oomen-ruijten report, which confirms the need for pension reform in view of the unfavourable evolution of the ratio of workers to pensioners. the resolution is in line with the recent eurobarometer survey showing the wisdom and maturity of european citizens, 73% of whom believe that they will have to work longer or save more for their old age. the prevailing idea of extending working life beyond 65 years is certainly appreciated by the population in different ways, but, for better or for worse, other levers will necessarily have to be activated. in my own country, belgium, where the employment rate of older workers is among the lowest in the european union, there is an urgent need to encourage older workers to stay longer in the labour market.
in writing. - ageing is on the rise, the crisis is forcing member states to cut back. but ageing must not lead to a new european debt crisis. and the member states that are cutting back must not do so rashly. the resolution stresses that the first pillar of the pension system is the most important. this implies a healthy national budget balance. it goes without saying that a steady income is a guarantee against falling into poverty. i also welcome the recognition of pension rights for women and the emphasis on greater gender equality, with the fact that older people should not be discriminated against in the labour market. the resolution also gives due consideration to the portability of accumulated pension rights. no one works for the same company or even in their own country for the rest of their life. it is fundamental in a united europe that such rights can be transferred. the report also calls for the commission to take the necessary steps to ensure that the eu's social security system is fully functional.

in writing. food prices have reached historic highs. this increase has led to food insecurity for millions of people, destabilized the world economy, and led to riots and social movements. the international community has committed itself to halving world hunger by 2015 as part of the mdgs. ensuring that every human being has adequate and regular food is not only a moral imperative, it is the fulfillment of a fundamental human right. this inalienable and universal right was affirmed at the acp-eu jpa plenary session in kinshasa last december. while the commission must honour its commitments to the developing countries and the least developed countries, it must also promote a strong and sustainable cap that is responsive to the needs of european farmers. i share the concerns of the latter, who, because of the fall in incomes due to rising production costs and price volatility, are not benefiting from the increase in food prices. effective and coordinated action is needed to address these problems. we cannot accept opulence and waste when the tragedy of hunger is growing.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on the increase in food prices because no one can be satisfied with the situation which has prevailed for months and which affects primarily small farmers and consumers. grain prices have even surpassed the 2008 highs, when high food prices caused unrest in countries such as haiti and egypt. if the responses must be primarily global and coordinated with the fao, they must be extended to the european level where price stability is an objective to be achieved. i therefore welcome the adoption of sensible proposals such as reducing food waste and the request to the commission to restrict trading in food commodity derivatives to investors with a direct link to agricultural markets. all these measures are in support of a strong and sustainable european agriculture. commissioner cioloş was just reminding us yesterday that europe is not here to subsidize agrofuels, but to give priority to the use of arable land for food production, a logic that is more elementary than that!
in writing. - food security policy is defence policy par excellence. any country that fails to provide its people with safe and affordable food and its farmers with a reasonable standard of living is headed for instability and food riots. the right to food is a basic and fundamental human right. the text before us rightly emphasizes the need for a multidimensional approach. ensuring food safety has links with more effective action to combat climate change, with improved development aid, with the development of other trade structures, with greater transparency in commodity markets and with measures to combat speculation. i would have liked to see the text strengthened even further, by calling for the creation of an independent global agency to strictly regulate speculation in food commodities. the greens also wanted to point out the necessary actions to reduce food waste: twenty to 30 percent of crops are already lost during sowing and harvesting. in developing countries, half the crop rots because it is not stored or transported. consumers and distributors in developed countries throw up to 40 percent of food products untouched into the trash. unacceptable and unethical! finally, i do not think that food should be part of the wto debate. food can never be a commodity. i will never!
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this joint resolution which highlights the main factors behind the current surge in food prices, namely the rise in oil prices, the growing production of biofuels which is eating up huge areas of agricultural land, the increasing frequency of climate disasters and speculation on the markets. the question is no longer to provide food at the best price, but to make the most of it. according to the fao, food prices reached a historic high in january, and it is estimated that when food prices rise by 1%, the nutrition of an additional 16 million people is at risk. so the rising prices are becoming a huge challenge for developing countries, which already spend almost three quarters of their income on basic foodstuffs. we therefore fear a social and political situation even more dramatic than during the "hunger riots" of 2008. europe has a fundamental role to play in ensuring global food security. let us hope that the g20 ministers, who will meet in paris next june, will find solutions to combat the volatility of food prices.
author. - mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, since the beginning of february new clashes have broken out between the cambodian armed forces and the thai armed forces on the border near the preah vihear temple, the surrounding area of which is claimed by both countries. there are casualties on both sides and more than 3,000 residents near the fighting zone have been evacuated. in 1962, based on french historical maps, the international court of justice of the un recognized cambodia's rights to the preah vihear temple and the adjacent territory. however, thailand has never accepted this decision. in addition, some areas of the border were not demarcated, which already caused several armed incidents in 2008 and 2009. in 2008, the temple's inclusion on unesco's world heritage list also provoked outrage from thai nationalists. although a memorandum of understanding on the demarcation of borders was signed in 2000, the nationalists of the thai pad are calling for its revocation as it is considered too favorable to cambodia. i would like to highlight in particular the action taken by indonesia, the current chairman of asean, which has offered to play the role of mediator in this conflict. on monday, the un also urged the two countries to observe a permanent ceasefire but did not plan to send peacekeepers to the area. i hope that these two countries can finally settle the question of this territory peacefully and stop taking thousands of people who want to live in peace hostage.
for the greens/efa group mr president, why are we talking about innovative resources? did we suddenly get rabies from the taxis? of course not! as you know, we must put public finances back on a sustainable footing, which means responsible spending, of course, but it also means fair, efficient and sustainable revenue, and as you know, the tax systems that are in place in europe today do not meet these criteria. they do not guarantee governments the means to carry out their public service missions: we think of education, research and social cohesion. they have not been able to stem the growth of inequality in europe and they continue to encourage activities that are destructive of both the environment and social cohesion. whether it is a question of taxing the financial industry, obtaining a fair contribution from large companies, implementing a climate-energy contribution or effectively combating tax fraud and evasion, you know that only at european level can we put in place effective solutions. action at member state level has become ineffective. we are tired of hearing that all this is impossible, that unanimity is needed. what do you want? it's too complicated. without joint action, it will not be ten years before any member state of the european union is able to return to sustainable public finances. what is on the table in economic governance, since that is what it is all about, is to say to the member states: 'cut off your spending arm by tying your other arm, the revenue arm, behind your back', and this is what is called a competitiveness pact. i'd like to see you fight with one arm cut off and one arm tied. i believe that the podimata report opens up avenues which will indeed make it possible to answer the tax question and i therefore hope that this parliament will be able to adopt it.

in writing. i welcome the vote on this report for which i had been appointed fictitious rapporteur for the epp. for the 500 million or so citizens we represent, we had to learn from this crisis to be able to respond better in the future to a possible new pandemic threat. the text voted yesterday is a very good compromise in terms of health cooperation, independence and transparency. the failure of genuine health cooperation between member states required a constructive and practical approach, involving the following actions. strengthened cooperation between member states and better coordination between member states and european institutions to ensure a more effective response to future pandemics. the clarification of the roles of the european health risk management structures. the request for a review by who of the definition of criteria for triggering a global pandemic alert. evaluation of the vaccination and communication strategies implemented in the member states to better restore citizens' confidence. the creation of a mechanism for collective procurement of vaccines by member states to avoid disparities. publication of declarations of interest of experts advising european public health authorities to avoid any conflict of interest.
in writing. − the handling of the h1n1 influenza, declared a pandemic by the world health organisation, in 2009 and 2010 was not transparent. this is addressed in the 'h1n1 management assessment report'. i particularly welcome this report because it provides for full transparency of medicines used in the event of a medical emergency and a pandemic. the member states have acted alone in ordering and using the vaccines. in this context, it is important to evaluate the strategy for the increase of vaccines and to seek a joint procurement of vaccines by member states in the future. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work is a very important one.
in writing. some do not support a financial transaction tax (ftt) at european level as it would create distortions of competition in financial markets to the detriment of europe. i don't think a tax of just 0.01% on these transactions will scare investors away from the world's largest financial market. if we are to count on the g20 to take this initiative at the global level, we will wait forever... i am therefore pleased that the amendment tabled by the s&d group for this ttf at european level has been adopted. it would create a resource estimated at 200 billion a year which would enable the union to finance its budget properly, even though some members of the council are already announcing their intention to restrict it, despite the added value of european spending. the crisis, which was caused by financial market players, is used as an argument by our right-wing leaders to call for budget cuts, especially in social spending. the european citizens would therefore be paying for faults that are not their own. this ttf would reintroduce social justice in european decisions, by consolidating public finances at the expense of those that have weakened them. so the timing was very timely.
in writing. i welcome this vote on the financial transaction tax because the european parliament calls on the union to put this taxation system in place without waiting for a possible decision to this effect at world level. the european union has the largest financial sector in the world. so she has to lead the way. according to various studies, the introduction of a 0.05% tax on transactions would generate some €200 billion in annual revenue to finance recovery and development cooperation, and protect the environment, while discouraging financial speculation. i am also convinced that such a tax is necessary at international level: the union must encourage its partners to adopt regulations on financial taxes. if this tax is implemented only within the european union and not at international level, by europe's main financial competitors, the union's finances will be severely disadvantaged. i hope that a compromise can be reached on this point at the g20 under the french presidency.
in writing. the global economic and monetary crisis of 2007 revealed the major weaknesses in the regulatory and supervisory framework of the global financial system. i have been at the forefront of the fight in the ep for innovative finance by setting up a working group on the feasibility of a tax on international transactions. i am convinced that the latter would not only help to regulate the financial sector effectively by limiting purely speculative actions but would also help the poorest, especially the developing countries, and among them the least developed countries, to achieve the millennium development goals and to take the necessary measures to deal with climate change. a financial transaction tax at european level could generate a potential revenue in the union of around eur 200 billion per year and nearly usd 650 billion per year globally. if we could make coherent progress at european level by applying a tax on international financial transactions, we would maintain the strong message we sent in december 2010 when we adopted the recommendation entitled 'the financial, economic and social crisis: recommendations on measures and initiatives to be taken'.
in writing. - i voted today again in favour of the introduction of a financial transaction tax (ftt) and also agreed that if the world fails to impose an ftt, the eu should take the first step. we had to seize this momentum and curb the greed of the financial and banking sectors. the european union is the world's largest financial market and europe can play a leading role in this. a financial transaction tax can provide member states with sufficient revenue to balance their budgets and keep their economies running. in addition, as the revenue potential of a ftt of 0.05% is close to eur 200 billion in the eu and usd 650 billion worldwide, this tax could be an important part of the solution in the search for new and sustainable sources of revenue. a ftt can curb speculation and stabilise markets, create incentives for long-term investment, increase transparency by making every transaction traceable and ensure that financial actors bear their share of the costs of the crisis. the report also calls for a more detailed examination of the possibilities of issuing euro bonds and of the introduction of a carbon tax.
in writing. i was keen to support the report by edith estrela on reducing health inequalities between and within the eu member states. simply because it shows a very wide range of persistent inequalities in this area within the union. these inequalities, which are unjust, are the result of multiple economic, environmental and lifestyle factors, but also of difficulties in accessing health care, either in economic terms or in terms of the "poor distribution of medical resources" in certain territories of the union. although health policy remains (for the most part) a national competence, we meps must push our member states to continue their efforts to tackle socioeconomic inequalities and therefore disparities in health care. member states must ensure that vulnerable groups (disabled people, the elderly, migrants... and women!) can effectively benefit from equitable access to health care. the emphasis should also be on prevention and health information in coordination with civil society organisations.

in writing. - the link between international trade, development and agricultural policy is undeniable. european agriculture is increasingly having difficulty exporting products to the world market, as prices are low there and production costs are higher in the eu. this continuing trend will continue to have a negative impact if no support programmes are provided for agriculture. i therefore welcome this owninitiative report, which provides for compensation for farmers if further opening up of the internal market to imports would lead to losses for farmers. the agreements negotiated by the eu with third countries are not problematic in themselves, but the sum of these agreements makes it difficult to maintain high standards in the eu. the commission's owninitiative report therefore calls for greater coherence between the eu's agricultural policy and its common commercial policy. in this context, i support the call for the commission to carry out an impact assessment for trade agreements and to publish it before the start of negotiations.

on behalf of the alde group. madam president, first of all, i think it is still fair to say that after years of not accepting the idea of economic union, we are finally accepting the idea of economic union alongside monetary union, which is still a step forward - except for mr farage, of course - but for everyone else it is still a step forward. however, madam president, i think the term used is wrong. what does "covenant" mean? a pact is an agreement between states. we don't need an interstate agreement. we need a community act, an initiative at the level of the european union and not a pact between the member states, which is intergovernmental in nature. so the term is not well used, the word is wrong. second, the method. there's no need for anything at the intergovernmental level. intergovernmentalism has never worked in the european union. the lisbon strategy was an intergovernmental strategy and it failed. the stability pact, when germany and france failed to comply with its rules in 2003-2004, proved that the intergovernmental method was not the right one. we must use the community method. thirdly, i believe that what is on the table, mr president of the commission, is not enough or is rather directed towards very specific measures. the competitiveness pact between mrs merkel and mr sarkozy consists of six specific measures. for example, in the matter of pensions, it is the age of retirement, and the pension system is much more complicated than that. it is not just the age of retirement, it is also the number of years of contribution, the pre-retirement schemes, whether or not there is a second pillar. so what we need is not six specific measures in an intergovernmental pact, which will never exist or work. what is needed is broad economic governance (pension systems, labour market, wage policy, taxation policy) in the european union which is, in fact, decided by the commission and which, by a convergence code - that is the word you used - is given to the member states to apply the rules contained in the convergence code. that's what we need as soon as possible. my request is very simple. i have seen the paper of 25 february which you drew up with the president of the council. i think it is now up to the commission to prepare its own initiative. we have to do it now. you still have time in the coming weeks to prepare these community acts on economic governance and convergence and to table them on the council's table and on the european parliament's table. it will then be up to us to decide and to support you in this, but i think we are on track for the time being. in this document of 25 i have it here what i read is monitoring by the heads of state and heads of government, the concrete commitments undertaken by the heads of state and heads of government. that's not how it's gonna work. it is not the states and the prime ministers who will control themselves! it has never worked, it will not work in the future! finally - member of the commission. − mr president, the eyafjallajökull eruption in iceland in april 2010 had an enormous impact which required the eu to act urgently. the commission therefore proposed immediate actions to coordinate the eu’s position and to strengthen the regulatory framework. this makes europe a stronger partner at a global level. the commission is actively engaged in practical work to refine the existing volcanic ash avoidance methodologies in aviation. for example, the commission has launched a specific call under the seventh framework programme called ‘technology support for crisis coordination for the air transport system following major disrupting events’. in parallel the european aviation safety agency (easa) is preparing rules for air-worthiness requirements and risk assessment for safe flight in airspace with volcanic contaminants. from an operational perspective, an approach has been developed in close cooperation with the easa. this approach reflects practices in other parts of the world. the guiding principles are as follows: first, the airline is responsible for the safety of its operations. before operating in airspace contaminated by volcanic ash, the airline must produce a safety risk assessment and have it accepted by its supervising authority. this process must be repeated when important changes occur. second, the airline must show that the information sources it uses in its safety risk assessment are correct. it also has to show its own competence and capability to interpret such data correctly. before starting operations, the airline must obtain from the manufacturers specific information regarding the susceptibility of the aircraft to the effects of airborne ash and the impact of such ash on its airworthiness. this must be reflected in the safety risk assessment. in dealing with disruptive events such as this, a key element is collaborative decision-making between member states and industry. to ensure comprehensive and coordinated actions, the commission, together with eurocontrol, established a european aviation crisis coordination cell, following the council of transport ministers meeting of 4 may 2010. since its creation, the cell has met on several occasions to develop its structures and procedures. to test and verify its timely functionality, this cell will be part of a volcano exercise planned for 13 and 14 april 2011 under the auspices of the un’s aviation body, the icao. the volcanic ash crisis highlighted the crucial importance of the single european sky. the commission has therefore accelerated its implementation via, for example, the adoption of the ses performance scheme and the associated eu-wide performance targets, the adoption of implementing rules for network management functions, the designation of the network manager, the adoption of implementing rules and guidance material for the functional airspace blocks, the nomination of the former mep mr georg jarzembowski as the functional airspace blocks coordinator and the expected finalisation by april 2011 of the extension of the easa’s competence for safety regulation in the field of air traffic management. let me therefore conclude by saying that the commission is continuing to work on these very complex and technical issues. the commission is working together with easa, icao, member states and industry to ensure the safety of european airspace.

vice-president of the commission. − madam president, i would like to thank parliament and the rapporteurs in particular for supporting the commission on these important agreements. all three have been strongly supported by the committee on transport and tourism. on the us agreement, let me start by thanking the rapporteur, mr zasada, for his very positive recommendation in relation to the outcome of the negotiations with the united states on a second stage air services agreement. you will remember that the aim of the second stage discussions was to facilitate the normalisation of the transatlantic market and extend the scope and depth of the excellent aviation relationship established through the implementation of the first stage agreement, in place since march 2008. i now want to mention the key elements of the second stage aviation agreement. the second stage agreement creates the prospects for additional investment and market access opportunities. it also further strengthens the framework of cooperation on the environment, social protection, competition and security. on the environment, the agreement establishes a clear framework for tackling local and global challenges. the agreement seeks to reduce the security burden on passengers, airlines and airports across europe. for the first time in such an aviation agreement, the need to balance market access opportunities with strong social protection has been recognised through a commitment to implementing the provisions of the agreement in a way which does not undermine labour rights. on the commercial front, europe has gained further rights, including immediate access to the ‘fly america’ programme with the exception of defence. the second stage agreement is not perfect. like you, i would have liked to have seen an immediate and irrevocable change to the us laws governing ownership and control of its airlines. this has not been possible, but we were able to secure a commitment from the united states to work towards reforming these rules in the future. as part of the agreement, the eu and the united states have committed to the goal of removing the remaining market barriers in industry, including those that limit airlines’ access to global capital. let me now turn to the agreement with canada. my thanks go to the committee on transport and tourism, and in particular to ms ţicău. this ambitious agreement is designed to achieve complete opening of the markets for traffic rights and investment, at the same time reaching an unprecedented level of regulatory convergence and cooperation between the authorities. with respect to market access, the agreement comprises the full range of traffic rights and investment opportunities: this means 100% ownership and control. it is done through a phased market opening in four phases. among its multiple benefits for both sides, it is also worth noting the establishment of a level playing field for the industry, as well as common or compatible standards for safety, security and air traffic management. last but not least, i am convinced that by removing existing regulatory restrictions this agreement will lead to a substantial increase in passengers and generate various consumer benefits and the creation of new jobs. on vietnam, let me also start by thanking the rapporteur, mr riquet, for his support for this horizontal agreement. currently, we have negotiated 45 such horizontal agreements with partner countries worldwide. on 4 october 2010, during a visit to the european union, the vietnamese prime minister signed the agreement, which represents an important step towards strengthening aviation relations between the eu and vietnam. the horizontal agreement will restore legal certainty to our aviation relations with vietnam by bringing the bilateral air services agreements between 17 member states and vietnam into line with eu law. most importantly, it will remove nationality restrictions in bilateral air services agreements between eu member states and vietnam. it will thereby allow any eu airline to benefit from the existing bilateral agreements between vietnam and the member state. thank you very much for your attention. i am looking forward to the debate.
i am speaking on behalf of the ppe group. the commission has already made a number of proposals. i would also like to thank the rapporteurs for their reports. the epp welcomes these agreements. it means that in this case one replaces almost 27 different agreements that could have been in these areas with one single agreement. technical harmonization is also an important point for us. this harmonization increases safety not only for the operation itself but also for the passengers. the opening up of markets and cooperation at european level should be treated in the same way on both sides. it is important to emphasize that the agreement with canada can be regarded as almost exemplary, while the agreement with the united states still leaves some expectations unfulfilled. i also think that the fact that we - and this is what will shape all future agreements - will have to review these agreements on social and environmental matters on a regular basis is not fulfilled, because simplification at economic level must also mean that we can influence not only the european market but also the global market through these agreements. the agreement also benefits the passengers themselves. the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the rules on the protection of the environment are respected. in conclusion, i would like to say that we welcome these agreements because, as i said, they will in effect replace the 27 by a single agreement. this is also a clear indication that we will soon be dealing with seven, or perhaps even three, airspaces in the context of aviation safety and the implementation of the single airspace, rather than the 27 we have at present. this will also facilitate the negotiation of these agreements.
