in writing. the report i voted for concerns the agreement signed with georgia and is fully in line with the european union's neighbourhood policy and common airspace with its neighbouring countries. the agreement aims to create a level playing field between all air carriers by allowing the gradual opening of the market through access to routes and capacity.
in writing. since georgia gained its independence in 1992, the european union has repeatedly expressed its willingness to maintain close relations with its eastern neighbour. this agreement on a common airspace is part of the desire to maintain lasting relations on various strategic issues. a common airspace will ensure safety and efficiency and the conclusion of this agreement will mean increased mobility for european citizens. in addition, maintaining regular contact with georgia on a wide range of subjects will also make it easier for us to deal with certain economic and political aspects which will be decisive in the long term, such as the opening up of markets.
in writing. 2010 was a year of unprecedented papy boom in belgium: more than 100 000 workers were admitted to the pension scheme. i welcome the invitation this report addresses to member states to recognise the importance of integrating migrants. immigration is a natural phenomenon. the history of mankind is the history of migration. zero immigration does not exist, has never existed and will never exist. in our time, it is no longer possible to spare a thorough reflection on the problem of migration. all countries are affected by the movement of people, whether as countries of origin, transit or destination. migration is a positive reality. they not only enrich the economies but also the culture and society of the countries of transit and destination. migration is a natural phenomenon that must be accompanied, modelled and made positive. in a europe where the regions are increasingly important, it is also important to remember that the structural funds earmarked for them can be used to achieve such an objective. unfortunately, this is not the case at present, as only 9% of the appropriations have been used.
in writing. demographic change is one of the major challenges facing public authorities, both at european and international level. the ageing of the population, the importance of migration flows, exodus from rural areas to urban areas. these demographic changes are one of the major challenges of the future. the report i voted for today calls in particular on the commission to improve its 'demographic vulnerability index' and to recalculate it every five years in order to better identify the regions of europe that are particularly exposed to demographic change. this is only the first step in managing these inexorable changes.
in writing. i supported the agreement between the polish presidency and the european parliament delegation on the prohibition of short selling on sovereign debt. it seems important to me that, following the decision taken by some member states (germany, france, belgium, etc.), the european union should 'clean up' the jungle of financial instruments which destabilise the markets and reduce the monetary funds available to finance the real economy. the creativity of experts is indeed limitless. as here, with this possibility given to financial institutions to buy a credit default swap without owning the underlying asset, for example a greek government bond. applied to the real economy, it's a bit like giving a citizen the opportunity to take out fire insurance on his neighbor's house with a clear interest in playing the arsonist. the temptation of the worst! the european parliament is seeking to bring about a 'return to normalcy' by adopting this regulation. the commission has already proposed a number of amendments to the proposal, including a number of amendments to the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work.
in writing. this directive 2005/26/ec applies to any national of a member state of the european union who wishes to pursue a regulated profession whether as a self-employed person or employed person in a member state other than the one in which he obtained his professional qualification. in practice, the recognition process based on professional experience is still too cumbersome and time-consuming for both the competent authorities and the professionals. i therefore welcome the adoption of this report because it aims at: (1) simplification for citizens in the sense that the length of the procedure will be reduced through the use of modern communication technologies, better centralisation of information and clarification of definitions, particularly as regards the temporary and occasional provision of services; 2) to update existing provisions (in particular by means of the classification of economic activities in line with scientific and technical developments); the commission has also proposed that the member states should be able to apply the principle of equal treatment to all workers in the same occupation.
in writing. professional mobility is a key element in stimulating economic growth, making the labour market more flexible and addressing demographic deficits in some regions of the european union. however, the freedom of movement of persons within the european union and the right to recognition of professional qualifications and competences can only be effective when the indirect obstacles which currently exist have been reduced to a minimum. the recognition of diplomas and professional qualifications is a fundamental condition for the establishment of a genuine internal market and for everyone to enjoy the benefits of this freedom of movement. all initiatives to facilitate crossborder mobility should therefore be encouraged. an effective way of enabling the free movement of professionals would be to reduce the total number of regulated professions in the union, although classification may be justified on grounds of consumer protection, in particular for medical, legal or technical professions. paid traineeships by graduates from other member states should be encouraged and it should be ensured that the professional experience gained during the traineeship is recognised in the home member state.
in writing. the adoption of the report on the recognition of professional qualifications is excellent news for the european worker: simplification and relaxation of the rules for the recognition of professional titles for a faster process, strengthening of cooperation between states, creation of a european professional card allowing easy access to information... are the main objectives. these proposals will ensure greater mobility and freedom for workers and guarantee the respect of citizens' rights. this arsenal of measures will still need to be supplemented by essential safeguards to ensure balanced recognition of the multiple qualifications existing in the eu and to guarantee a reliable service by the professional, especially in the field of health. the challenge is enormous: the length of studies, internships, language training, there are as many formats as there are states for each learning. modernization of reconnaissance will have to be done cautiously but safely, as more than 50% of young people are willing to work abroad, according to eurobarometer (may 2011). there is still a long way to go before full recognition of vocational qualifications, despite european progress in the equivalency of qualifications and diplomas.
in writing. i welcome the commission's initiative to launch a consumer protection programme. it is necessary to ensure that consumers enjoy a high level of protection throughout the european union. consumers must have access to useful, targeted and comprehensible information without, however, creating additional burdens for businesses. special protection should be ensured for groups of consumers who are particularly vulnerable because of their mental or physical health or age. it is also important to educate consumers from an early age. in view of the growth of financial services and electronic commerce, measures are needed to define good practices for electronic commerce and rules covering electronic means of payment. we must continue to combat unfair business practices such as false advertising and aggressive business practices such as harassment. consumer confidence is a powerful economic driver for both traditional and electronic commerce and therefore needs to be reinforced by clear and effective measures.
in writing. the adoption of the report on the new strategy for consumer protection is good news. the european parliament supports the ambitious guidelines of the european commission. these aim to make consumer choice considerably easier by giving priority to more and more information on products (e.g. clearer labelling, transparent and comparable information on prices) and placing particular emphasis on food safety (information on pesticide, chemical content, etc.). other priorities include reducing consumer inequalities, a low-carbon economy and protecting children from advertising in the fight against obesity. the citizen has the right to demand exhaustive information in order to consume in an informed manner. globalisation, environmental awareness and technological developments have dramatically changed consumer habits. it was therefore important to reform the priorities of the community strategy for consumer protection. this report seeks to define a better, coherent legal framework for a safe and transparent environment that takes into account the concerns of europeans.
in writing. sensitive vote this afternoon on online gambling, with so many conflicting interests and visions between member states, national lotteries and the many players involved in this frenetic and particularly lucrative online business, estimated at 10 billion euros, 10% of all gambling in the european union. i am pleased that the rapporteur has struck the necessary balance in an area which is by definition transfrontier and sensitive when it comes to the protection of minors, the fight against illegal gambling, prevention and also addiction. two in particular: - i voted for paragraph 22 in support of the continuation of the many infringement procedures against european law launched by the commission in the face of quasi-monopolies, sometimes in times immemorial. if i understand their freezing back when there was a legal vacuum, they must be reasonably examined and the european commission must play its full role as guardian of the treaties, much to the chagrin of those who hoped to see these procedures simply abandoned. - i also supported paragraph 45, to protect sporting events from outside commercial exploitation and to give the organisers a right of ownership, a good measure which could help to combat sporting fraud.

in writing. as a signatory to the alternative resolution to the tabajdi report on bee health and the challenges facing the beekeeping sector, i can only deplore the vote by the european parliament this afternoon. a vote that favours the interests of fertiliser and pesticide producers at the expense of bee colonies which are disappearing in many parts of europe. the european parliament has a pressing duty to protect bees and other pollinators so important for the planet and biodiversity. the explanatory memorandum says: '84% of plant species and 76% of food production in europe depend on pollination by bees, whose economic value is much higher than the value of honey produced and estimated at eur 15 billion per year in the eu.' i therefore still hope that a genuine european support plan will be adopted, opening up real prospects for the beekeeping sector. to achieve this, it is imperative to ban the most toxic pesticides such as neonicotinoids and to propose a new agricultural model based on crop rotation and the rational use of pesticides.

in writing. cluster munitions pose a grave threat and cause excessive suffering to civilians, especially children, long after the end of military conflicts. the draft text concerning protocol vi to the convention on certain conventional weapons is not compatible with the convention on cluster munitions. the draft protocol prohibits only cluster munitions manufactured before 1980, provides for a long transition period, authorizes the use of cluster munitions with a single self-destruct mechanism and allows the use of cluster munitions with a non-explosive rate of less than 1%. the protocol will therefore undermine the clear and solid international law established by the convention on cluster munitions, which completely prohibits such weapons. i fully share the call on all member states of the european union to refrain from adopting, approving or ratifying any protocol authorising the use of cluster munitions prohibited by the convention. it is important that member states and candidate countries which are not parties to the convention accede to it as a matter of urgency and that the signatory states ratify it as soon as possible.
in writing. the european parliament voted unanimously this afternoon on the resolution on the prohibition of cluster munitions. parliament called on the member states not to deviate from the convention on cluster munitions, which is currently signed by 110 countries, and in particular to reject protocol vi, which will be discussed in geneva this month at the 4th review conference of the convention. this protocol vi could allow the use of cluster munitions produced after 1980 under certain conditions. the opportunity to recall the enormous humanitarian damage these weapons can cause: 98% of their recorded victims are civilians, and 5% to 40% of the cluster munitions do not explode on impact, thus becoming antipersonnel mines. millions of land mines and explosive remnants of war "sleep" in fields and along roadsides in more than 100 countries today, especially in cambodia, afghanistan, angola, and vietnam. they kill or maim for years after the end of a conflict and also create another handicap, that of not being able to exploit the land. this is a major obstacle to development in countries which often desperately need it.

vice-president of the commission. − mr president, i have been invited to discuss the preparations for next week’s european council with you on behalf of president barroso. the european council will, of course, take place in an extremely challenging economic and political environment. its focus will inevitably be on the economic situation and on the measures we have proposed to restore confidence in the euro area and the european economy. it is clear that our room for manoeuvre is now much more constrained than two years ago. to respond to the current situation, the commission has utilised the current treaty’s scope to the maximum and proposed forceful measures to complete the economic and monetary union. economic governance is being strengthened and mechanisms to address the financial crisis have been already been put in place. last wednesday the commission adopted the growth and governance package, which consists of three parts. the annual growth survey spells out our view of the policy priorities in the coming 12 months to restore macrofinancial stability and boost sustainable growth. two proposals for new regulations will further reinforce economic and budgetary surveillance in the euro area. the feasibility study on stability bonds examines the potential benefits for financial stability of jointly issued bonds and the preconditions for their possible introduction. the annual growth survey launches the next european semester of economic governance by setting out the commission’s views on the challenges and priorities for next year. this survey is being published at a time when the eu is going through the most challenging times of its history. it sets the following priorities for 2012. first, to continue with fiscal consolidation, which has to be differentiated across countries, as we agreed in october. we also have to pay more attention to the impact of consolidation on growth. in this respect, it is essential to analyse carefully which expenditure we can reduce and how we can raise revenue in the member states. second, that normal lending to the economy has to be restored. it is necessary to strengthen the banking sector via appropriate regulation and recapitalisation and set up credible financial backstops for banks and sovereigns in order to break the negative feedback loop between the two sectors. third, structural policies are key to reviving growth at the current juncture, when macroeconomic policies are heavily constrained. this means that structural reforms have to be stepped up, especially in services, network industries, the public sector and the digital economy. fourth, unemployment and other social consequences of the crisis have to be tackled. reforms are necessary to make labour markets more flexible and conducive to job creation. the final priority of the survey is to modernise public administration at all levels in the member states and in the union. you may say that some of these priorities are not new. this is correct and it is deliberate. we have already made so many commitments that now we have to really focus on their implementation and concrete results. the discussions of the annual growth survey will culminate in the march european council, after which the national programmes are prepared in the light of the guidance from the heads of state and government. in parallel, you in the european parliament should also debate the annual growth survey and make your views known before the work on member states’ programmes starts. to my mind, that is a very important opportunity for the european parliament to influence policy-making in the member states in this regard. to conclude on the annual growth survey, i want to underline the following once more. without swift and determined implementation these priorities will do none of us any good, nor help achieve sustainable and inclusive growth. i have full confidence that in the european parliament you will help accelerate the adoption of what is currently on your desks in the codecision procedure. as part of the package we also proposed two regulations based on article 136 for the euro area member states. these present a major step forward in euro area fiscal and economic integration. they build on the ‘six pack’; they complete the european semester with rules for the second part of the year and establish a link between intergovernmental financial assistance and treaty-based surveillance. the first regulation proposes the introduction of binding rules for balanced budgets into national legislation, preferably at constitutional level. it also requires independent forecasts to be used as the basis of budgetary plans and draft budgets. but, most importantly, it proposes tight monitoring of national budgets, which you have been calling for. we propose a harmonised budgetary timeline with draft budget laws to be submitted to the commission by 15 october every year. the commission will then assess these draft national budgets against the country specific recommendations and against possible edp recommendations. should the draft clearly not be in line with the recommendations, the commission can ask for a new draft. the commission is ready to present its opinion in the national parliament of the country concerned if requested. when a member state is in the excessive deficit procedure, the commission can issue recommendations for additional measures. the second regulation specifies the modalities for enhanced monitoring of euro area member states – those member states who are receiving financial assistance or are suffering from risks to their financial stability and to that of the euro area as a whole. it allows enhanced surveillance of a country that is considered to be at risk with regard to financial stability, even without a programme. finally, it proposes that the commission will have the right to propose to the council to recommend a member state to seek financial assistance if the member state concerned is posing a risk to financial stability, especially that of the euro area or europe as a whole. this should be done on the basis of the commission’s analysis in liaison with the european central bank. this proposal stems from recent experience, as we have seen that this has posed a genuine problem to the financial stability of the euro area. the fragmented european sovereign bond market is currently under great stress. investors require substantial risk premiums on the sovereign bonds of some euro area member states. this situation has revived interest in jointly issued euro area bonds to create a large and liquid bond market in europe. as part of the deal on the ‘six pack’ between the european parliament and the council, the commission presented a green paper on stability bonds last week. its key findings are, firstly, that jointly issued stability bonds would be likely to produce substantial benefits in terms of reducing and stabilising borrowing costs for member states by providing better shock resilience for the financial sector and improving market efficiency over time. secondly, however, as common bonds would reduce the market discipline of individual member states, their introduction would only be meaningful on the condition that euro area economic governance were to be substantially further strengthened. the ‘six pack’ constitutes the foundations for reinforced economic governance and last week’s proposals represent a further step in the direction of stronger economic governance. but we would have to go far beyond these reforms to facilitate a safe introduction of stability bonds, which would most probably require amendment to the treaty. before concluding, let me say a few words on treaty change. let us be clear: a treaty change cannot offer an immediate contribution to the solution to the current crisis. but it is true that, by working to embed stricter discipline and stronger governance into the euro area in particular, we may help to prevent a future crisis by creating a real stability union. the president of the european council was asked, with the presidents of the commission and the euro group, to identify possible steps on further reinforcing economic convergence within the euro area, including exploring the possibility of limited treaty changes. these deliberations are ongoing and an interim report will be presented to the european council. the commission’s view is that any treaty change should be based on the principle of one union, based on the current institutional framework, which is clearly exemplified by the community method. european integration can only be achieved by a single legal framework of one union. that is the best way to build a real stability union, in fact a true economic union. equally importantly, only the community method can guarantee consistency between european economic monetary policy and all other eu policies as well as the completion of the single market. that is the guarantee of the fair and just treatment of the member states and eu citizens. i trust both the european parliament and eu member states will stick to this and be ready to justify the benefits of the community method vigorously in future negotiations too. furthermore, in the event of any of revision of the treaties, balance has to be maintained. we all know that there will be diverging views – some will want to put more weight on stability, while others might wish to place more emphasis on stimulating growth. some will call for more solidarity and others will want more discipline. it will be essential and extremely important to incorporate all these elements in future work so that the end result will be a balanced set of rules ensuring both stability and solidarity, which are at the heart of the european social model. i can second what the minister said as regards energy policy, that this is a key element on the agenda. likewise the european council will take important decisions concerning the schengen accession of bulgaria and romania. let me express the commission’s view on this. it is very clear: we expect that the council will take the decision to lift internal border controls with romania and bulgaria without any further delay. we fully support the efforts made by the presidency for a compromise solution. splitting into two phases the decision on lifting internal border controls is feasible and politically sound. the second stage – the decision on the lifting of internal border controls at land borders – can then be taken without undue delay. finally, a word on enlargement and the accession treaty of croatia, which is very close to my heart and to which commissioner stefan füle will return after this debate. real progress has been made during the last year with all countries – progress in which the cooperation with the european parliament plays a significant role. the commission has already given its favourable opinion on croatia’s accession and we hope that the vote tomorrow will pave the way for the council’s decision and the signature of the treaty on 9 december. but i will leave the details to my colleague and will just say that this is a historic turning point for croatia and a very important benchmark for accession by the rest of the western balkans to the european union. let me conclude. in terms of the european economy and economic policy, we have indeed arrived at the point in time where serious choices and commitments have to be made. the economic and monetary union will either have to be completed through much deeper integration or we will have to accept a gradual disintegration of over half a century of european integration. this is a choice that needs to be consciously taken by the governments of the euro area member states and by all european citizens and their representatives in the national parliaments and here in the european parliament. our choice is clear. it is a choice for an ever closer union for the sake of sustainable growth and job creation in europe and thus for the sake of legitimacy and, not least, for the sake of the future of european unification. this is what is at stake. i trust you will also make the choice for european unification and for these objectives, because that is what our citizens expect. in writing. more than 6 million adolescents leave the school system without a diploma. it is a problem common to all member states and one which is growing rapidly, which is why the european parliament has dealt with the matter by voting this afternoon on a resolution on school drop-outs. recent figures show that 52% of young people who have left school without a diploma are unemployed and will add to the battalion of 5.5 million unemployed young people. this is simply unacceptable and untenable, in the long run, if we want to preserve social cohesion and intergenerational solidarity in our western societies. this is why we should welcome the interesting proposals in the honeyball report: the extension of compulsory schooling from 16 to 18 years of age, and the creation of more 'second chance' schools, as the one-size-fits-all approach does not suit all young people in school. because reversing the dropout rate is not something that can be done by decree, and it requires investment in education. it is also necessary to give new value to technical courses and to ensure that a diploma gives the right to a job. right and not chance: this is the dilemma to be resolved in the field of education.

in writing. the code of conduct for meps adopted this afternoon responds to the need for greater transparency and clarity in our day-to-day work in the european parliament. it also responds to the recent scandals caused by a few colleagues who were paid to defend special interests, an unqualifiable attitude which was immediately denounced by the presidency of parliament and the national and european parties which were quick to exclude these black sheep. among the new rules: more transparency and control over members' declarations of financial interests, a clear definition of conflict of interest, the obligation to refuse any gift worth more than 150 euros, and the establishment of a peer review committee. however, and to quote a colleague who knows the meaning of the phrase: "just because you catch someone's hand in the jam pot, you don't have to ban jam". despite the strictest rules and punishments, you will not eliminate abuse. integrity is not a command, it's a practice. and it is above all a matter of moral duty, personal ethics, a sense of responsibility. these are all values that we don't compromise.
in writing. the euro crisis is closely linked to divergences between member states on their economic and fiscal policies. the establishment of a 'european semester' or 'economic governance' was therefore essential. this new tool for the coordination of the union's economic and budgetary policies is intended to verify the application of budgetary discipline by the member states and to monitor the proper implementation of the europe 2020 programme by ensuring that it has sufficient financial resources. with the introduction of the european semester, we have taken a further step on the road to european integration. however, it must be remembered that parliamentary debate on the broad guidelines of economic policy is the cornerstone of any democratic system. we cannot ignore the democratic debate. i therefore fully support mrs berès' call for full transparency on the amendments introduced after discussion with the member states on the country-specific recommendations.
in writing. according to the report published by who and unaids, 2.7 million people were infected with hiv in 2010 and 34 million people are living with hiv. prevention of hiv/aids through effective information is still essential. the condom, the only effective means of protection against hiv/aids, should be available free of charge or at low cost. similarly, anonymous and free testing should be at the heart of a european prevention campaign. efforts in sub-saharan africa, including rwanda, namibia and botswana, are to be commended, with an overall annual increase of 30% in the number of people receiving antiretroviral treatment. the economic crisis must not be a brake or a barrier to the application of new technologies and new approaches to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of hiv programmes.
in writing. on this world aids day, it is important that the european parliament sends a strong and consistent message. even with the extraordinary progress made so far in hiv prevention and testing, it is essential to remain vigilant and maintain a target of "zero spread" of the epidemic. this is the message that the european parliament is sending today, by adopting a resolution calling for more equitable access to testing, treatment and care, and thus reducing the number of hiv infections. more than 27 000 people are infected in europe each year, including 1196 in belgium in 2010, or more than three a day. while the impact of antiretroviral drugs is very effective - there are far fewer deaths from aids today - a relaxation of sexual vigilance or a trivialization of infection is not tolerable. hiv is very complex and still raises many questions, for example about the problem of co-infection, particularly with tuberculosis and viral hepatitis b and c. the european parliament resolution is part of an ongoing effort to find a much-anticipated vaccine.
in writing. since ukraine's independence in 1992, the european union has steadily developed bilateral relations with its eastern neighbour. the many resolutions which have recently been voted in parliament are in this direction. the association agreement between the european union and ukraine is naturally part of this positive and constructive logic. the conclusion of such an agreement should, beyond the shared economic benefits, lead ukraine to progress towards a state based on the rule of law, a state guaranteeing democracy and the fundamental rights of its citizens. democracy has complex requirements that go beyond the right to vote and the respect of elections. democracy requires the protection of rights and freedoms, respect for the rule of law, and the guarantee of free discussion and the encouragement of debate. it is above all freedom of opinion. the majority does not allow the tyranny of the majority. democracy is constructive opposition, a free and caring civil society, an independent press.
in writing. an effective customs union is one of the essential elements of the european integration process and forms the basis for the free movement of goods, economic development and growth in the internal market. to play their full role, customs must be modern, cooperative, responsive and efficient. to this end, member states must provide customs with sufficient resources, in particular for the development of computer systems, in order to achieve the necessary modernisation of customs. an effective customs policy plays a vital role in protecting intellectual property rights and in combating the illegal entry of counterfeit goods and products into the european market. it therefore improves safety and security for european consumers. the modernisation of customs procedures should not, however, create unnecessary burdens, especially for smes. the need for consistency in the management of the external borders of the european union is a necessity, and it is important to ensure greater harmonisation of customs control and sanction systems.

in writing. i voted in favour of this report because under the new legislation, anyone suspected of having committed a criminal offence will now have to be informed of his rights in a language he understands. this will ensure that eu member states provide any person arrested (or subject to a european arrest warrant) with a 'bill of rights' listing their fundamental rights throughout the criminal proceedings. this proposal is part of an overall legislative package to be presented in the coming years, which will aim to establish a minimum set of procedural rights to be granted in criminal proceedings in the union and to strengthen confidence in the single european area of justice - a whole programme! however, obstacles still remain, notably the need to take account of the different legal systems, and in particular the differences between civil law countries and so-called common law countries such as ireland and the united kingdom.

in writing. if there is one report i particularly welcome the vote on in this plenary session, it is this one! victims of crime who are protected in one eu member state will now enjoy similar protection when travelling to another european country, thanks to the new european protection decision rules. although measures to protect victims of crime already existed in the member states, they did not apply when the victim travelled to another country. it will now be done! this protection will cover, for example, victims of sexual violence, harassment, abduction, stalking or attempted murder, as the directive will protect against any act or behaviour by another person which could endanger in any way his life or physical, psychological or sexual integrity, as well as his dignity or personal freedom.
in writing. a major step towards establishing a genuine european area of justice was taken this afternoon. the european parliament has adopted a series of measures introducing enhanced european protection for victims of crime, who will be protected in the same way throughout the european union. priority will be given to victims of gender-based violence, harassment, abduction, stalking or attempted murder. although rules for the protection of victims already exist in each eu country, they are insufficient in that they do not cover victims on the move and therefore often leave them defenceless. this is therefore a real development for the victims and their families, whose dignity and integrity are guaranteed within the european union through judicial and police cooperation between member states. the point here is not to advocate a europe of shields, but to make a european area of protection for particularly fragile and vulnerable people a reality. this necessarily and practically requires simplifying access to justice for all and giving priority to defending the rights of victims over those of the accused.
in writing. the vote on this report will allow migrants from third countries legally working in the european union to enjoy rights comparable to those of eu nationals in terms of working conditions, social security and access to public services, under a new 'single permit' decided today. in addition, administrative formalities will be reduced by obtaining a work and residence permit through a single procedure. in addition to simplifying the procedures for residence and work permits, the single permit will therefore make it possible to grant a common set of rights to workers from third countries and to workers from the union. equal treatment of workers is at the heart of this directive, and i welcome its adoption.

on behalf of the alde group. mr president, on 1 january 2017, phosphates will therefore be excluded from dishwasher detergents. these are measures which many professionals and ngos have been awaiting and which confirm, in a way, the legislative arsenal of some member states, which have already banned these powerful cleaning products. phosphates, which are very effective as water softeners, are also pollutants, which disturb the water balance and therefore contribute to the eutrophication of european waters. i would like to thank very warmly our rapporteur, mr bill newton dunn, who, with wisdom and intelligence, together with the polish presidency and the commission, convinced us that it was right to extend this regulation to dishwasher detergents. i have two reservations about this agreement, however, and i will abstain - in my personal capacity, not on behalf of my group - when we vote tomorrow. two reservations which, it seems to me, are symptomatic of the state of mind in europe today. the first is that i do not think that the agreement takes sufficient account of smes, particularly those which manufacture phosphates. not far from my home, for example, near liège, the firm prayon - 780 direct jobs - is rightly concerned about the negative impact of this legislation on its business. clearly, the philosophy of 'think small first' is sometimes difficult to put into practice. second reservation and this has been said before, and it is common sense : ninety percent of our water eutrophication comes from sources other than dishwasher detergents. so with or without them, this pollution will continue. we need a real european leap forward: legislation not on the margins, as is being done here, but on the essentials, for better implementation of the directive on waste water treatment - this is obvious - and against intensive agriculture and the dumping of food waste, the real culprits when it comes to the degradation of european waters.

in writing. the aim of the directive is to give priority to product quality and consumer information. thus, the main name of the product should correspond to the predominant fruit and all fruits used should be mentioned in the list of ingredients. the illustrations on the packaging must not mislead the consumer as to the actual composition of the juice. the most important change for juices is the removal of sugar from the list of permitted ingredients. the aim here is to guarantee the quality of fruit juices and to promote health. it is also important that the consumer can clearly distinguish between the different product categories, namely, pressed fruit juices, fruit juices produced from concentrates and nectars. all these measures will have to be accompanied by specific and large-scale information campaigns to dispel the confusion which currently exists. finally, i welcome the fact that the specific nature of each national market is maintained by a clear product name and that the directive applies both to products manufactured in the european union and to imported products.

in writing. i voted today in favour of this report, which provides that detergents used in washing machines and washing machines must no longer contain phosphates. i remind you that phosphates are used in detergents to reduce the hardness of water and improve washing. however, when discharged into lakes and rivers, they promote the growth of algae that kill other aquatic species by depriving them of oxygen (detergent is the third largest source of phosphate discharge into surface waters, after agriculture and waste water, while laundry detergent is the largest source of phosphate in the detergent sector). from january 2013, phosphorus compounds used in washing machine products will not exceed 0,5 grams per wash. the rules will be extended to dishwashers from 2015. these new rules - and i welcome them - will undoubtedly improve water quality and protect aquatic life, which is under attack from phosphates discharged into waste water.

in writing. - i voted against the extension of the eu-morocco fisheries agreement because western sahara is not part of morocco. fishing in saharan waters is a violation of international law. the use of a bilateral agreement to fish in the waters of western sahara is contrary to international law. moreover, the moroccan security services, and not the saharawi population, strictly control fishing in the occupied western sahara. in addition to the fact that this agreement is clearly in breach of international law, an evaluation report by the commission also shows that the agreement is a huge waste of european taxpayers' money and contributes to the destruction of fish stocks. it is the most inefficient and wasteful of all the bilateral fisheries agreements in force. every euro invested in the total of 36 million euros paid out by the union to morocco every year yields a negative return of 83 cents! and the agreement does not contribute in any way to the development of the local fisheries industry. finally, the commission did not consult the european parliament nor did it adequately involve it in the negotiation process. finally, the rejection of this agreement is in line with the analysis of the legal service of the european parliament.
in writing. the many controversies surrounding the fisheries agreement between the european union and morocco seem particularly misplaced to me. in 2010, the commission asked morocco to assess the situation and what efforts could be made in the future to improve the fisheries partnership. morocco, a long-standing partner of the european union, has complied and proved that the fisheries agreement has been beneficial in terms of job creation throughout morocco and for the sahrawi population. in environmental terms, almost 40% of the financial contribution from the agreement is allocated to the conservation of fish stocks and the development of the fisheries sector. to establish a protocol in such unflattering terms with regard to our moroccan partner seems to be a serious mistake for the european union and its bilateral relations.
in writing. following the economic and financial crisis, the trend is towards a reduction in defence budgets among member states. what i wanted to draw attention to - and i am far from being a warmonger - is that uncoordinated cuts in the defence budgets of the member states of the union could lead to a decline in europe's military capability. i therefore believe that more integration and pooling of resources could be a solution, as there are many areas in which member states could optimise their resources, such as strategic and tactical transport, logistical support, etc. more initiatives for mutualisation and sharing are therefore needed in the areas of transport helicopters, aerial refuelling, maritime surveillance, unmanned aerial systems, protection against chemical, biological and nuclear hazards, satellite communication, etc. i am also convinced that the european defence agency (eda) should play a greater role, particularly in the context of eu-nato cooperation.
in writing. a defence europe is essential not only for ensuring its own security and the survival of its social model but also for being credible on the international scene. the crisis is leading member state governments to cut defence spending. that is why it is urgent and necessary to organise our defence effort by making economies of scale. to remain competitive and effective, we need to enhance our synergies, pool our capabilities, develop effective strategies that will enable the eu to be able to manage crises, whether in libya, the horn of africa or elsewhere. the eu and nato must deepen their cooperation. the european defence agency needs to be given a larger budget. europe can only be a reliable ally of the united states and a reliable partner for china if, as pierre defraigne says, it acquires its autonomy in foreign policy.
in writing. russia is one of the eu's most important partners in many respects. the many political and economic agreements signed with neighbouring russia show that the european union regards it as a key partner on the international scene. twenty years ago, the totalitarian regimes of central and eastern europe were falling. a great victory for democracy! however, we are currently facing a worrying situation. the last parliamentary elections were widely criticised for the respect of procedures and the transparency of the results. respect for democracy also depends on the holding of elections worthy of the name, freedom of expression, the presence of a free political opposition and freedom of association and demonstration. it is now up to russia to prove to its long-standing european partner that it is willing to move towards a state based on the rule of law.
in writing. the revision of the european neighbourhood policy seems both necessary and welcome in the light of the events of the past few months. the arab spring has put issues of great importance on the agenda. it seems to me essential to think about the establishment of a fair and accessible european asylum system that goes hand in hand with a european visa system. migration is a natural phenomenon linked to the human condition. the european neighbourhood policy, which has been reshaped, must create a favourable environment for partnerships with third countries in the sometimes dramatic situations affecting them. the european union would have much to gain by encouraging initiatives aimed at informing migrants of their rights but also their duties.

for the greens/efa group madam president, ladies and gentlemen, it is clearly the banks that today constitute the greatest threat to the functioning of the internal market and i would even say to the future of the european economy. indeed, some banking institutions have become too large and too important, giving them an unbearable market power. they are able to crush their smaller competitors and to absorb activities previously carried out by others - i am thinking of the activities of stock exchanges - in which they want to establish themselves as market places in place of the established stock exchanges. the biggest of these banks are not content to abuse their market power, they want to seize political power, and i think the most striking example of this was the reception of the head of deutsche bank at the summit of heads of state and government on 21 july, with the respect due to heads of state. how is that possible? because these large banks enjoy, on the one hand, the implicit guarantee of the taxpayer, as sophie in 't veld has said, but also, on the other hand, because the european central bank grants them a lender's guarantee as a last resort, in other words, guarantees them unlimited liquidity. it is striking that the same central bank, which finds it intolerable to give a lender's guarantee of last resort to the member states, finds absolutely no problem in giving the same guarantee to private institutions. i see this as the result of an ideological choice, which is to say that governments and states are inherently untrustworthy, while banks - big or small - are. it is clearly this ideological mold that we must break. too big to fail, systemic banks, simply shouldn't exist. too big to fail is too dangerous to exist! beyond the competition policy you are pursuing, mr almunia, which i believe has been successful, the texts we will adopt in 2012, the crd iv directive and the directive on banking crisis resolution, should, in my view, be an opportunity for us to reduce the market power of these banking institutions. that is where we will see whether we can find a majority in this house to bring the banking industry back to a size and practices more compatible with the general interest.
on behalf of the ecr group. – madam president, the cornerstone of eu competition policy has always been the elimination of obstacles to the free movement of goods, services, persons and capital. i am pleased to know that the european commission increasingly uses economic analyses when shaping competition policy, and i hope that it will continue to follow this course in the future; ultimately competition is about economics. a balanced approach to competition policy combines elements of both public and private enforcement. public enforcement is essential to fully achieve the goals of the single market and to ensure the enforcement of eu competition law by the commission and by the national competition authorities. private enforcement is compensatory in nature, in the sense that it promotes a personal interest in the private actor initiating it. however, private actions also help to pursue the public interest of deterrence. i mentioned at a meeting of the committee on economic and monetary affairs in october that, when it comes to collective redress, mr lehne behaves like a shadow commissioner for competition policy. the ecr group cannot support his approach of a horizontal instrument. we would like to see a system of access to national collective redress systems for those in other member states, based on a non-binding framework and specific sectoral measures. in the 2010 competition policy report i appreciate very much the emphasis on the need to discontinue as soon as possible the temporary state aid rules adopted in the context of the financial and economic crisis. furthermore, i strongly support the suggestion to the commission that it should take into account the impact, in terms of distortion of competition, of ecb liquidity support provided to banks during the rescue stage. finally, let me thank mr schwab, the rapporteur, for his good cooperation. i hope that we can continue to work together in the same constructive spirit.

in writing. parliament was consulted today on the proposal to include trade provisions for textile products in the partnership and cooperation agreement (pca) between the european union and uzbekistan. this bilateral agreement expired on 31 december 2004. although in practice trade in textiles between the union and uzbekistan has continued smoothly since 1 january 2005, this issue has acquired more political sensitivity than the strictly technical nature of the proposal would suggest. indeed, many allegations of forced labour have emerged, in particular allegations of child labour in the cotton production sector in uzbekistan. i therefore voted in favour of suspending the approval procedure so that the international labour organisation can carry out further investigations into the real situation of forced child labour in that country. first of all, i therefore demanded that ilo observers be allowed to monitor the situation of child labour and that concrete reforms be introduced to ensure that the practice of using forced child labour finally disappears!
